new.s: According to an APPSC (2007) question, most of the tribal languages of central and eastern India belong to which language family?
new.x: Most tribal languages of central and eastern India (Jharkhand-Odisha-West Bengal belt: Santhali, Mundari, Ho) are Austric. Dravidian covers only some central tribal pockets (Gondi, Kui, Kurukh); Sino-Tibetan is the language family of the North-East and Himalaya; Indo-Aryan is the family of the north, west and east plains.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Net migration is in-migration minus out-migration.
2. Counter-urbanisation refers to movement of people from urban to rural areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: net migration = in-migration minus out-migration. Statement 2 is correct: counter-urbanisation is movement from urban to rural areas. So 'Both 1 and 2' is right; '1 only' and '2 only' each leave out a true statement, and 'Neither' is wrong.
new.tq: Net = In - Out; counter-urbanisation = city to village.
